I've played this game quite a lot in the past before it was released to Steam. By no means was I good, especially since the game has a rather large learning curve. This learning curve comes from the fact that various joints must be manipulated to get results, but casual players (especially friends) will often find hilarity due to the manipulation of their characters sometimes in rather awkward positions. Multiplayer games are rather fast-paced compared to singleplayer sessions due to the timer which limits the time players can think before it runs out. Otherwise, various mods come with the game which adds plenty of PvP options (arena type, weapons, body sensitivity, etc.), or solo challenges (parkour, skateboarding, sports, etc.).

In terms of play by more seasoned/veteran players (not including myself), other players can find interest in the rather complicated techniques used to simulate real fights or complete parkour maps.

Overall, this game takes a long time to fully understand since the tutorial does not completely cover everything, but once players get past this, they'll find many challenges to overcome.

I think it's a lot of bang for your buck, honestly (especially since it's completely free.) It takes quite a while to get the hang of, but once you get it, you get super addicted to it: being able to make your own moves, parkour/freerunning, the array of different mods and the decking out of your Tori (character) make it interesting and new every time you play it.

Some cons though are that there are a few toxic people/kids that either get really salty, use annoying moves (such as the famous 'shovel' in aikido,) or both. I wouldn't consider it a con, but some people seem to think it's supposed to be realistic or even that it IS realistic. That's totally false. If you think of it that way then you're kinda missing out. And finally, that making moves can be confusing. I've seen some people say that they've gotten bored with it and that other people always use the same moves. I can't totally argue with that, but what I CAN say is that with enough practice and the right people you can have a really fun time with it.

Overall, I'd totally recommend this game.
